reviewed_by: Claude: callback stall watchdog, focused backend selection
reason: Provider turns parked in waiting_callback (subagent, reply or background-command waits) had no level-triggered recovery. The recovery tick now runs a stall watchdog (NEBULA_CALLBACK_STALL_SECONDS, default 20 min, bounded 60 s to 24 h): a satisfied but unwoken subagent/reply wait resumes; a stalled subagent/reply wait ends with the subagents' current state and the turn continues; a command wait past its own deadline is interrupted like an orphaned turn (effect outcome unknown) and resumed once by restart recovery. A second stall of the turn or its goal interrupts for the operator and pauses the goal. Working children, commands within their deadline and held projects are left alone. Session state now reports last_progress_at for open provider turns. Selected: the new regression file plus the subagent wait/resume, goal lifecycle and resume-metadata, goal auto-retry (shared clear-streak path), orphan and restart recovery (shared interrupt/auto-reconcile paths) and the session-state, approval-handoff and polling-cost suites that read session_state.
exclusions: No UI, frontend or native change: the UI does not render last_progress_at yet, so frontend, native and Playwright layers are empty. Harness turns and Butler are unchanged. The threshold is a Core environment variable, not an operator settings field, so the settings assistant catalog is unchanged. No full-suite approval.
